les: Van ys tot waterdamp en terug
kaps_punt: Verandering van die toestand: verhitting en verkoeling (verwydering van hitte) veroorsaak vastestowwe, vloeistowwe en gasse om hulle toestand te verander -- 'n soliede stof sal eerste verander na 'n vloeistof (smelt) wanneer dit verhit word en dan verander die vloeistof na 'n gas (verdamp) met verdere verwarming -- gas verander eerste na 'n vloeistof (kondensasie) wanneer dit afkoel word en dan verander 'n vloeistof na 'n soliede stof (vries) wanneer dit verder afgekoel word

items.bewering: Ys, water en waterdamp is alles water, en net die toestand verskil. Ys is die vaste stof, water die vloeistof en waterdamp die gas.
items.bron: USGS Water Science School, 'Evaporation and the water cycle' (https://www.usgs.gov/water-science-school/science/evaporation-and-water-cycle): water vapour is the gaseous state of water; Britannica, melting entry (https://www.britannica.com/print/article/591422). Volledig nagegaan in hierdie ronde.

items.bewering: Jy kan waterdamp glad nie sien nie, maar dit is tog daar.
items.bron: Scientific American, 'How does bathwater give off steam?' (https://www.scientificamerican.com/article/how-does-bathwater-give-off-steam/), University of Michigan physicist: visible plume is liquid droplets, the vapour is invisible; Science Buddies expert answer (https://www.sciencebuddies.org/science-fair-projects/ask-an-expert/viewtopic.php?p=59782): water in the gas phase is invisible. The absolute 'glad nie' holds: what people see as 'stoom' is condensed droplets, not the gas.

items.bewering: Hou 'n blokkie ys in jou warm hand en dit word water.
items.bron: Heat flows from the warmer body to the colder one (Wikipedia, 'Thermal equilibrium', https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thermal_equilibrium); ice at or below 0 C absorbs latent heat and melts (LibreTexts, 'Phase Change and Latent Heat', https://phys.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/University_Physics/Physics_(Boundless)/13%3A_Heat_and_Heat_Transfer/13.3%3A_Phase_Change_and_Latent_Heat).

items.bewering: Gooi daardie water in 'n bakkie en sit dit in die vrieskas. Later haal jy dieselfde water as 'n harde blok ys weer uit. Die blok het die vorm van die bakkie.
items.bron: Freezing is liquid to solid when heat is removed, a reversible physical change (Britannica melting entry, https://www.britannica.com/print/article/591422: freezing removes the heat melting absorbed); a liquid takes the shape of its container and the solid keeps that shape once frozen. Water expands slightly on freezing, but the block still has the container's shape.

items.bewering: Die water raak nooit weg wanneer sy toestand verander nie.
items.bron: A change of state is a physical change; no substance is created or destroyed (LibreTexts phase change, link above; USGS evaporation page: evaporated water exists as vapour in the air). Consistent with the lesson's own puddle example, where the water 'verdwyn' from sight but is said to be vapour in the air. Ice slowly sublimating in a freezer is also still water, so 'nooit weg' holds.

items.bewering: Twee dinge kan 'n materiaal se toestand laat verander. Die eerste is verhitting, en dit voeg hitte by die materiaal. Die tweede is verkoeling, en dit vat hitte van die materiaal weg.
items.blok: Hitte gaan in en hitte gaan uit
items.bron: LibreTexts, phase change and latent heat (link above): heating and cooling drive changes of state. Note for a person, not a fault: pressure also changes state (LPG is held liquid in a gas bottle by pressure; NIST, https://www.nist.gov/document/b-008pdf). The sentence does not say 'only' and matches the CAPS bullet's own framing, so it is incomplete rather than false.

items.bewering: Verkoeling is hitte wat weggaan en nie koue wat inkom nie.
items.blok: Hitte gaan in en hitte gaan uit
items.bron: Science Buddies, 'Heat and cold' (https://www.sciencebuddies.org/science-fair-projects/ask-an-expert/viewtopic.php?p=47492): heat flows from warmer to cooler; 'cold' is not a substance that flows. Ohio State 'Beyond Penguins' misconception material (https://beyondpenguins.ehe.osu.edu/?p=2919) lists 'cold flows in' as a misconception (page could not be opened; corroborated by the search summary and Science Buddies).

items.bewering: 'n Vrieskas maak nie koue nie, maar dit vat net hitte uit die kos weg. Daardie hitte gaan by die vrieskas uit in die kombuis in. Die hitte raak nie weg nie, maar dit beweeg net na 'n ander plek.
items.blok: Hitte gaan in en hitte gaan uit
items.bron: iFixit, 'How a Refrigerator Works' (https://www.ifixit.com/Wiki/How_a_Refrigerator_Works) and Physics Forums thread on fridge thermodynamics (https://www.physicsforums.com/showthread.php?p=4456142): refrigerant absorbs heat inside and releases it to room air through the condenser coils. The room actually receives slightly more heat than was taken from the food, because the compressor's work adds heat too; the lesson does not deny this, and 'net' reads as 'merely', so the mapping holds.

items.bewering: Party dinge het meer hitte in as ander. Selfs 'n blokkie ys uit die vrieskas het nog hitte in. Dit het net minder hitte in as 'n koppie warm water.
items.blok: Ook 'n koue ding het hitte in
items.bron: NSTA lesson plan 'Warming water' (https://www.nsta.org/lesson-plan/warming-water): all objects possess thermal energy, even very cold objects like ice cubes, and warmer water has more. For a normal ice cube against a cup of hot water this holds on mass and temperature alike. Terminology note for a person, not a fault: in physics 'heat' strictly names energy in transfer and what an object 'has in' is thermal (internal) energy (Science Buddies, 'Heat and cold', link above). The lesson uses 'hitte in' for thermal energy throughout; read that way every statement in the block is true and the comparison does not mislead.

items.bewering: Sit 'n warm bord op 'n koeler tafel neer en wag 'n rukkie. Die bord word kouer, en die tafel word warmer.
items.blok: Ook 'n koue ding het hitte in
items.bron: Wikipedia, 'Thermal equilibrium' (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thermal_equilibrium): heat flows from the hotter to the colder body through the available pathway.

items.bewering: Die bord gee net 'n deel van die hitte weg en nie alles nie. Die hitte hou op om te beweeg sodra die bord en die tafel ewe warm is. Albei het dan nog hitte in.
items.blok: Ook 'n koue ding het hitte in
items.bron: Wikipedia, 'Thermal equilibrium', and Miniphysics, 'Thermal Equilibrium' (https://www.miniphysics.com/thermal-equilibrium.html): at equal temperature there is no NET heat flow; both bodies retain thermal energy. Strictly, energy still passes both ways at the particle level and 'no net flow' is the precise form, and in a real kitchen both also exchange heat with the air; at Grade 4 'hou op om te beweeg' is the accepted simplification and leads nowhere false.

items.bewering: Verhit 'n vaste stof genoeg en dit verander in 'n vloeistof. Hierdie verandering se naam is smelt.
items.bron: Britannica, melting entry (https://www.britannica.com/print/article/591422): melting is a solid becoming a liquid when heat is applied. Tested as a set with the block 'Nie elke materiaal verander so nie': stated alone the first sentence is universal and would be false for wood, but the lesson itself names the exception (wood burns rather than melts), so the lesson as a whole does not teach that every solid melts.

items.bewering: Die vaste stof verloor sy eie harde vorm en begin vloei.
items.bron: Solids have a fixed shape and liquids take the shape of their container (Britannica melting entry; LibreTexts phase change, links above). 'Harde' is loose for butter, which is a soft solid, but the claim that the solid loses its own shape and flows is true for every example given.

items.bewering: Op 'n warm dag smelt 'n blokkie ys en word water. Botter smelt in 'n warm pan en loop plat oor die bodem.
items.bron: Ice melts above 0 C (LibreTexts phase change, link above). Butter melts over roughly 32-35 C (The Physics Factbook, 'Melting Point of Butter', https://hypertextbook.com/facts/2003/JessicaCheung.shtml; Michigan State University Extension, https://www.canr.msu.edu/news/buttergate, on butter's melting range), well below a warm pan.

items.bewering: Sjokolade smelt in jou warm hand, en roomys smelt in die son.
items.bron: Library of Congress, Everyday Mysteries, 'Why does chocolate melt in your hand?' (https://www.loc.gov/everyday-mysteries/chemistry/item/why-does-chocolate-melt-in-your-hand/): chocolate melts between about 30 and 32 C (86-90 F), below body temperature, so the hand melts it (page itself returned 403; content confirmed through the search result quoting it). Ice cream is frozen and melts in warm sun; same heat-flow principle.

items.bewering: Kerswas smelt naby die warm vlam.
items.bron: HowStuffWorks, 'How does a candle work?' (https://home.howstuffworks.com/question267.htm) and Royal Institution candle chemistry sheet (https://www.rigb.org/sites/default/files/attachments/candlechemistry_infosheet_0_1.pdf): the flame's heat melts the wax at the wick's base. Paraffin candle wax melts at about 46-68 C.

items.bewering: Hitte laat die verandering elke keer gebeur.
items.bron: Melting is endothermic: heat must be absorbed every time (LibreTexts phase change, link above). 'Elke keer' refers to the examples in the block, all of which are heat-driven.

items.bewering: Verhit 'n vloeistof nog verder en dit verander in 'n gas. Ons noem hierdie verandering verdamp, en water word dan waterdamp.
items.bron: USGS, 'Evaporation and the water cycle' (link above): evaporation turns liquid water into water vapour and needs heat energy. 'Verdamp' is the Afrikaans term for liquid to gas, as used in the lesson's own CAPS bullet.

items.bewering: Water hoef glad nie te kook voordat dit kan verdamp nie.
items.bron: USGS evaporation page (link above): water still evaporates, more slowly, even at its freezing point; Wikipedia 'Evaporation' mirror (https://wikipedia2007.classicistranieri.com/e/v/a/Evaporation.html): laundry dries outdoors below the boiling point.

items.bewering: 'n Plas water op die pad verdwyn stadig in die son. Daardie water het verdamp, en dit is nou waterdamp in die lug. Dieselfde gebeur wanneer nat klere aan die wasgoeddraad droog word.
items.bron: USGS evaporation page (link above); Wikipedia 'Evaporation' (link above) on clothes drying outdoors by evaporation. Some puddle water may also soak into the ground, but evaporation in the sun is the process the sentence names and it is correct.

items.bewering: Hoe warmer die dag is, hoe vinniger verdamp die water.
items.bron: USGS evaporation page (link above): evaporation is slow at freezing and easy near boiling, i.e. faster when warmer. Wind and humidity also matter, so a humid hot day can be slower than a dry windy cool one; as an 'other things equal' statement it is correct.

items.bewering: Koel 'n gas genoeg af en dit word weer 'n vloeistof. Ons noem hierdie verandering kondenseer.
items.bron: USGS evaporation page (link above): condensation occurs when saturated air is cooled, using a glass of ice water as the example; WeatherOnline, 'Dew Point' (https://weatheronline.cz/reports/wxfacts/Dew-Point.htm).

items.bewering: Gooi water en blokkies ys in 'n glas. Klein druppels water vorm gewoonlik aan die buitekant van die glas. Daardie water kom uit die lug en nie deur die glas nie.
items.bron: TERC Inquiry Project, Condensation Concept Cartoon (https://inquiryproject.terc.edu/curriculum/curriculum5/concept_cartoon/condensation/): droplets come from vapour in the air, and 'seeped through the glass' is a known learner misconception. 'Gewoonlik' is right: it depends on the air's humidity relative to the glass's temperature (dew point).

items.bewering: Die lug teen die koue glas verloor hitte en koel af. Die waterdamp in daardie lug verander in klein druppels. Daar was dus al die tyd water in die lug.
items.bron: WeatherOnline, 'Dew Point' (link above): all air has some water vapour in it, invisible until it condenses; air cooled below its dew point loses vapour as liquid. The causal chain (air cools against the glass, vapour in it condenses) is correct.

items.bewering: Blaas jou asem teen 'n koue ruit en druppels vorm ook daar. Jou asem bring sy eie water saam, en dit werk selfs op 'n droë dag.
items.bron: OpenStax College Physics exercise (https://collegephysicsanswers.com/openstax-solutions/air-human-lungs-has-temperature-370circtextrmc-and-saturation-vapor-density-0) and Deranged Physiology CICM answer (https://derangedphysiology.com/main/cicm-primary-exam/past-papers/2012-paper-2-saqs/question-3-0): air in the lungs is saturated with water vapour at 37 C (about 44 g per cubic metre), so exhaled breath carries its own water regardless of room humidity and condenses on a surface cooler than its dew point; ScienceNotes on breath condensing (https://sciencenotes.org/why-do-you-see-your-breath-when-its-cold/).

items.bewering: Koel 'n vloeistof nog verder af en dit word 'n vaste stof. Hierdie verandering se naam is vries.
items.bron: Britannica melting entry (link above): freezing is the reverse of melting and requires removing the same heat. (Helium does not freeze at normal pressure even near absolute zero; irrelevant at Grade 4 and to every example in the lesson.)

items.bewering: Sit 'n bakkie water in die vrieskas en laat dit daar staan. Die water verloor hitte en word 'n harde blok ys. Die ys hou nou sy eie vorm, en dit vloei nie meer nie.
items.bron: LibreTexts phase change (link above): freezing releases latent heat, i.e. the water loses heat; solids keep their own shape.

items.bewering: Die gesmelte kerswas koel af en word weer hard. Die naam van hierdie verandering bly egter steeds vries.
items.bron: Freezing (also called solidification) is any liquid-to-solid change on cooling, at whatever temperature; molten wax setting is a standard example (Britannica melting entry, link above; Merriam-Webster, 'freezing point', https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/freezing%20point: the temperature at which a liquid solidifies). Calling it 'vries' although the wax is not cold is scientifically correct.

items.bewering: Verhitting loop van 'n vaste stof na 'n vloeistof na 'n gas. Verkoeling loop dieselfde lyn terug van gas na vloeistof na vaste stof. Dit is een lyn, en 'n materiaal kan in albei rigtings daarop loop.
items.bron: Mapping checked. True for water and for every material in the lesson at everyday pressure (LibreTexts phase change, link above: melting and vaporisation absorb heat, condensation and freezing release it, and each is reversed by the opposite). Note for a person, not a fault: some solids skip the liquid (dry ice, mothball naphthalene) and frost forms straight from vapour (LibreTexts, 'Sublimation and Fusion', https://chem.libretexts.org/Courses/Pasadena_City_College/CHEM_001A%3A_General_Chemistry_and_Chemical_Analysis/12%3A_Liquids%2C_Solids%2C_and_Intermolecular_Forces/12.06%3A_Sublimation_and_Fusion). The CAPS bullet printed in the lesson states the same one-line sequence, and the lesson's examples never lead a learner to a sublimating material, so the 'line' does not mislead within the lesson's reach.

items.bewering: Dieselfde water kan smelt, verdamp, kondenseer en weer vries. Daarna kan dieselfde vier veranderings weer van voor af begin.
items.bron: All four are reversible physical changes of water (USGS evaporation page; LibreTexts phase change, links above).

items.bewering: Smelt: 'n vaste stof word 'n vloeistof wanneer dit verhit word. / Verdamp: 'n vloeistof word 'n gas, en hitte laat dit vinniger gebeur. / Kondenseer: 'n gas word 'n vloeistof wanneer dit afkoel. / Vries: 'n vloeistof word 'n vaste stof wanneer dit verder afkoel.
items.bron: Tested as a set. The one contrast the four draw, that melting is tied to heating while evaporation is only sped up by heat, is true: evaporation happens below boiling (USGS, link above) while ice melts only when it gains heat. 'Verder afkoel' for freezing against 'afkoel' for condensing is correct for water (condensation can occur well above 0 C, freezing at 0 C). Definitions agree with Britannica and LibreTexts (links above).

items.bewering: Smelt en verdamp: hitte gaan in die materiaal in. / Kondenseer en vries: hitte gaan uit die materiaal uit.
items.bron: LibreTexts, 'Phase Change and Latent Heat' (link above): melting and vaporisation are endothermic, freezing and condensation exothermic. Holds for evaporation without heating too: the evaporating water takes heat from its surroundings (USGS: evaporation is 'a net cooling').

items.bewering: Baie materiale om jou kan van toestand verander, maar party doen dit glad nie. Verhit 'n stuk hout en dit brand eerder as om te smelt.
items.blok: Nie elke materiaal verander so nie
items.bron: Wonderopolis, 'Why do some things burn while others melt?' (https://wonderopolis.org/wonder/why-do-some-things-burn-while-others-melt): wood's polymers decompose (a chemical change) at about 250-300 C, before any melting point, and the gases burn. 'Glad nie' is correct for wood as a material; the water inside wood does evaporate, but the wood itself does not melt.

items.bewering: Verhit 'n eier in 'n pan en dit word hard in plaas van sag.
items.blok: Nie elke materiaal verander so nie
items.bron: Wellesley College Chem 106 notes on irreversible denaturation (https://blogs.wellesley.edu/chem106/category/week-7) and New World Encyclopedia, 'Denaturation (biochemistry)' (https://newworldencyclopedia.org/entry/Denaturation_(biochemistry)): heat unfolds egg proteins, which bond into a solid network that does not revert on cooling, a chemical change rather than a change of state. Tested against the set: the contrast with butter, chocolate and wax (which soften and flow when heated) is true. Note for a person, not a fault: the lesson elsewhere names 'word hard' as freezing for wax, and gives the learner no stated reason why a hardening egg is not a change of state; that is a teaching gap, not a false claim.

items.bewering: toestand: Of 'n materiaal 'n vaste stof, vloeistof of gas is.
items.bron: Britannica melting entry and LibreTexts phase change (links above): the three everyday states of matter. Plasma is omitted, which is appropriate at Grade 4.

items.bewering: verhitting: Om hitte by 'n materiaal te voeg sodat dit warmer word.
items.bron: Correct as a definition of heating. Note for a person, not a fault: while a material is actually melting or boiling, added heat does not raise its temperature (MSU Open Books College Physics, 'Phase Change and Latent Heat', https://openbooks.lib.msu.edu/collegephysics/chapter/phase-change-and-latent-heat: ice stays at 0 C while it melts). The lesson nowhere claims the temperature rises during a change of state, so a Grade 4 learner is not led wrong.

items.bewering: verkoeling: Om hitte uit 'n materiaal weg te vat sodat dit kouer word.
items.bron: Science Buddies 'Heat and cold' (link above): cooling is heat leaving. The same latent-heat caveat as 'verhitting' applies during freezing (MSU Open Books, link above); not a fault at this level.

items.bewering: smelt: Wanneer 'n vaste stof warm word en in 'n vloeistof verander.
items.bron: Britannica melting entry (link above). Read alone: 'warm word' means 'is warmed / gains heat'; melting ice stays at 0 C and never feels warm, but it is being heated, so the entry is true. Read alone it also implies every solid melts when warmed, but as a definition of the word 'smelt' (what happens when a solid does melt) that is not a claim about all solids.

items.bewering: verdamp: Wanneer 'n vloeistof in 'n gas verander. Dit gebeur vinniger wanneer die vloeistof warmer is.
items.bron: USGS, 'Evaporation and the water cycle' (link above).

items.bewering: kondenseer: Wanneer 'n gas afkoel en weer in 'n vloeistof verander.
items.bron: USGS evaporation page (condensation when saturated air is cooled); WeatherOnline 'Dew Point' (links above).

items.bewering: vries: Wanneer 'n vloeistof afkoel en in 'n vaste stof verander.
items.bron: Britannica melting entry; Merriam-Webster 'freezing point' (links above).

items.bewering: waterdamp: Water in die vorm van 'n gas wat niemand kan sien nie.
items.bron: Scientific American bathwater article; Science Buddies; WeatherOnline 'Dew Point' ('Water vapor is an invisible gas') (links above). Read alone the entry is true: the visible white 'steam' is condensed droplets, not the gas.

opsomming: Elke kontroleerbare bewering, ook die begrippe, die lys as 'n stel en die vyf toestandsblokke saam gelees, klop met bronne; niks is weerspreek of onseker nie, en drie aanvaarbare vereenvoudigings is vir 'n mens aangeteken sonder om foute te wees: 'hitte in' staan vir termiese energie, die 'een lyn' laat sublimasie (droë ys, ryp) uit soos die KABV-punt self, en die les se kontras met die eier is waar maar verduidelik nie waarom die eier se verharding nie vries is nie.
